Subject: Re: Intermittent 429s on /v1/generate (Feb 25 morning)

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the artifacts. Diego and I ran a reproduction pass against the exact request shape and timing you provided. Summary of what we found so far: 

- We examined token and request rate metrics for the cluster and the specific tenant key you used; no global or per-key rate limits were reached at the time windows you shared.
- The packet capture shows that the client TCP session sent a burst of duplicate requests (same payload repeated) during a short window — likely retries from the client side without exponential backoff. Those duplicates can make it look like a high instantaneous QPS from a single connection.
- Server-side logs for req_a2b1 show the first request was accepted and processed; the later duplicate requests returned 429 because our per-connection concurrent request guard rejected them as we hit per-connection capacity (this happens when multiple in-flight requests arrive from the same socket). In short: the platform handled the first one; subsequent rapid duplicates were rate-limited by design to protect downstream workers.

Action items we've taken: 
- Marked the tenant traffic pattern as reviewed and increased the per-connection concurrent request limit slightly for the short window as a temporary measure so your rollout can continue.
- Diego has an internal change underway to improve logging so we can show which request instance was accepted vs throttled (INF-1245).

Next steps for you (small client-side changes):
- Ensure your SDK is configured to avoid immediate request duplication (add jitter + backoff on retries).
- Reduce aggressive per-connection concurrency in the SDK (we can share recommended settings).

If you'd like, we can also do a short call to walk through the pcap — happy to schedule. Does Friday 09:00 PST work?

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Support Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Intermittent 429s on /v1/generate (Feb 25 morning)

Hi Alex —

Following up to close out the investigation. We validated the following and have closed out the incident on our side: 

- Reproduction attempts from our lab (including replaying your pcap) produced the same pattern: initial request processed, near-immediate duplicate attempts were rejected (429) by per-connection concurrency protection.
- No backend worker errors or broader cluster throttles were observed. Token and CPU metrics were within normal ranges for the timeframe.
- We applied a narrow, temporary per-connection concurrency increase for your tenant to avoid blocking your rollout while you implement client-side backoff. That change was reverted after your team confirmed reduced duplicate retries.

We're classing this as "not a platform bug" — root cause: client retry behavior creating transient duplicates that resemble a spike and trigger per-connection safeguards. Recommendations:
1) Add exponential backoff with randomized jitter on retries.
2) Limit simultaneous requests per TCP connection (we recommend < 8 concurrent generation requests).
3) Share a follow-up if you continue to see 429s after changes and we'll re-open the investigation.

I'll attach the short analysis we used to verify the behavior (attached to this thread). Thanks for the quick cooperation — and please re-open if anything else pops up.

Best,
Diego Fernández
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime
